Hi Jamie -

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a shared plan:

Summary of what we covered
- Use-case: customer support assistant + semantic search/reranker for KB.
- Primary integration path: Redwood hosted API during pilot, potential Dedicated pool for production.
- Key concerns: auth & data isolation, embeddings + reranker latency, and rate limiting behavior under burst traffic.

Technical follow-ups (what we'll deliver)
1) SDK quickstart + auth: sample Node/Python snippets showing API key (Bearer) usage and short-lived token pattern if you want to rotate keys from your KMS.
2) Routing and fallbacks: recommended policy to route to Dedicated endpoints for heavy batching; fallback to hosted model variant with lower capacity if Dedicated exhausted.
3) Structured output & tool-calling: example of JSON schema enforcement + tool calling for KB lookup to keep hallucination surface low.
4) Rate limits, quotas, retries & idempotency: detailed guidance on 429 handling, exponential backoff windows, idempotency via request_id header, and recommended retryable vs non-retryable codes.

Proposed next steps
- I will send a short integration playbook (SDK snippets + auth examples + retry policy) - aiming EOD tomorrow.
- If your infra team wants a deeper architecture sync, Marissa can run a 30-min tech call next week to walk the arch diagram and edge cases.

Attachments: architecture diagram (arch PDF) + example retry policy (txt).

Anything I missed? If that looks right, I'll include a couple of sample requests showing embeddings -> reranker flow and a sample idempotency header in the playbook.

Best,

On Tue, Jun 30, 2026 at 9:42 AM Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acme-corp.com> wrote:
> Thanks Ben - good summary. Couple of clarifying questions from our side before the playbook:
> 
> 1) Auth: we plan to use our KMS + short-lived tokens. Does Redwood support exchanging our OIDC tokens for short-lived Redwood tokens (so we don't store long-lived API keys)?
> 2) Rate limits: what's the per-second/per-minute baseline on hosted vs Dedicated? We expect bursts from search traffic (hundreds of requests in seconds).
> 3) Retries: curious about idempotency. When you say request_id header - should we generate a UUID per user interaction, even for multi-request flows (e.g., embeddings + reranker)? Any guidance for batching to keep ids consistent?

Great questions - answers below. Sticking to short bullets so your infra team can skim:

1) Auth & short-lived tokens
- Yes: Redwood supports an OIDC-based exchange flow via our private deployment or partner-managed tenancy. For hosted customers we offer a short-lived token exchange using an inbound OIDC assertion and our token endpoint (no permanent API key stored). I'll include a Node/Python snippet showing the exchange + how to pass the Bearer token in SDK calls.
- If you need KMS-wrapping, we can accept tokens signed by your KMS and optionally validate via introspection.

2) Rate limits & quotas (baseline estimates)
- Hosted (pilot tier): soft limit ~ 50 req/s per account with burst to ~200 req/s with adaptive throttling.
- Dedicated (small pool): configured for sustained throughput - typical reserved pool supports 500-2,000 req/s depending on GPU sizing.
- Quotas are configurable at the route/model level; we'll propose a draft policy for your expected traffic pattern.

3) Retries + idempotency guidance
- 429 handling: treat 429 as retryable with exponential backoff + jitter. Start with an initial backoff of 200ms, multiply by 2, cap at 10s. Add full-jitter (random between 0 and backoff) to reduce thundering herd.
- Retry vs non-retryable: 5xx transient (502/503/504) -> retryable with capped attempts. 400-series (other than 429) -> do not retry. 409 often indicates conflict - retry only if operation is known to be idempotent.
- Idempotency: include X-Request-ID: <uuid> for each independent user action. For multi-step flows (embeddings -> reranker) we recommend:
  * Per user interaction: generate a parent UUID for the overall interaction.
  * For batched/sub-requests: include child UUIDs but also include parent UUID in headers (e.g., X-Parent-Request-ID) so we can correlate and dedupe server-side.
- Server-side dedupe: Redwood will accept X-Request-ID and ignore duplicate mutating operations seen within 5 minutes by default (configurable). For non-mutating generation calls, dedupe isn't necessary but can help with billing visibility.

4) Batching & embeddings/reranker notes
- For embeddings: batch requests to reduce per-call overhead; aim for 2-8 KB per request for optimal throughput on our runtime.
- Reranker flow: compute embeddings, store vector IDs, then call reranker with top-K candidates (we send an example payload in the playbook). Keep reranker calls stateless so retries are safe.

5) SDK recommendations
- Use our official SDK (Node/Python) which implements: automatic retry with exponential backoff and jitter, request_id injection, and transparent token refresh when using short-lived exchanges.
- We'll include code to show how to surface retryable vs terminal errors to your observability.

Attachments: I attached the architecture diagram and a short retry policy snippet.

Next steps
- I'll send the playbook (SDK + sample requests + retry policy) within a few hours.
- Marissa - can you take the lead on scheduling a Thurs AM tech sync with Acme infra?

Thanks - let me know if you want deeper numbers on latency percentiles for embeddings+reranker.

Best,
Ben
